claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi can form a single-phase FCC alloy.
A gradient or hierarchical grain structure can systematically tune local deformation mechanisms in CoCrFeMnNi.
Such tuning can produce a stable plastic-deformation response across a wide temperature range.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has homogeneous chemistry.
CoCrFeMnNi can be processed into a grain-size gradient extending from submicrometer grains to coarse grains.
Multi-step rolling and annealing can deliberately produce the proposed grain-size gradient in CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed material response applies from approximately 77 K to approximately 900 °C.
A gradient microstructure forms grain-boundary and dislocation structures that provide sites for slip or twinning at different length scales.

The active deformation mechanisms in CoCrFeMnNi vary with temperature, with slip and deformation twinning operating at lower temperatures and slip becoming associated with partial recrystallization above about 700 °C.
The graded microstructure enhances work hardening at lower temperatures.
The graded microstructure stabilizes plastic flow at higher temperatures.
Fine and coarse grains distribute slip, twinning, and boundary-mediated deformation between different microstructural regions.
The alloy can retain relatively high strength over a broad temperature range.
The alloy can retain relatively high ductility over a broad temperature range.
Microstructural heterogeneity increases tolerance to plastic-strain localization.
Uniform-grained CoCrFeMnNi has consistent strength and ductility but lacks the dislocation-pathway tuning provided by grain-size gradients.
Near or above 1000 °C, or under rapid strain rates, grain growth or phase evolution may diminish the benefits of the gradient structure.
The contributions of short-range ordering and twin-mediated deformation in different temperature regimes remain unresolved.
